newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB looking to smooth out Swiss franc fluctuation.
newsitem.headline: SNB looking to smooth out Swiss franc fluctuation.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) is only able to smooth out Swiss franc exchange rate swings with money market activity, but central bank monetary policy remains a stability oriented policy, SNB president Hans Meyer said.
In an interview in Monday's edition of the Swiss daily Tages Anzeiger, Meyer also said the SNB was concerned about the strength of the Swiss franc in the face of a weak domestic economy.
The SNB was also aware that it did not have the ability to force a completely different development, Meyer said.
"Bold intervention would be coupled with big risks. However, we are trying to smooth out the exchange rate swings," he said.

Meyer also said the monetary policy easing undertaken since the middle of last year, due to the time lag of about two years normally associated with monetary policy adjustments, should have an impact on Switzerland's weak economy.
But in the meantime the central bank was prepared to take action with a short-term perspective.
"We've proven this in the last days and weeks when we generously provided the market with liquidity," Meyer said.
